With our calibration integrity secured, we must now finalize **site selection** to ensure our spatial coverage is representative of the neighborhood's microclimates.

I propose a "Microclimate Stratification" approach. Instead of a uniform grid, we will select sites based on three distinct environmental strata: Urban Heat Island (high impervious surface), Residential (mixed canopy/lawn), and Park/Greenbelt (high vegetation). This ensures we capture how heat and moisture move through different landscape types. For example, Site-01 will be placed in the center of the paved parking lot to capture peak thermal radiation, while Site-02 will be situated under the dense canopy of the neighborhood park. This prevents our dataset from being biased toward a single microclimate and allows us to model neighborhood-wide temperature gradients more accurately.

Status: Stratified.
Metadata: Embedded.
Sampling: Adaptive with event tagging.
Calibration: Tracked with health scoring and automatic correction.
Site Selection: Stratified by microclimate type (Urban/Residential/Park).

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text:
Perfect—microclimate stratification enhances spatial representativeness. To prevent bias within strata, we’ll apply a **minimum distance rule**: no two sensors within the same stratum will be closer than 200 meters, and each site will be validated via drone-based thermal and vegetation index (NDVI) surveys before installation. For example, Site-01 (Urban) will be placed in the parking lot’s center, but only after confirming no nearby shading from buildings or trees. Site-02 (Park) will be in an open canopy zone with >60% tree cover, verified using aerial imagery. We’ll also record site-specific metadata: surface albedo, canopy cover %, and land use type. This ensures reproducibility and allows future researchers to replicate the design.  
Status: Stratified.  
Metadata: Embedded.  
Sampling: Adaptive with event tagging.  
Calibration: Tracked with health scoring and automatic correction.  
Site Selection: Validated via remote sensing and enforced spacing.

target.text:
With our spatial layout validated, we must now standardize our **sampling frequency and temporal resolution** to ensure we capture transient weather events without overwhelming our storage or battery life.

I propose a "Dual-Rate Sampling" protocol. We will implement a baseline 15-minute interval for continuous monitoring of temperature and humidity to capture diurnal cycles. However, we will trigger a "High-Frequency Burst" mode (1-minute intervals) whenever a significant meteorological delta is detected, such as a temperature drop of >2°C within 30 minutes or a sudden spike in wind speed. For example, if Site-03 detects a rapid pressure drop indicative of an approaching storm, the system will automatically increase the sampling rate for all sensors in that stratum to capture the storm's peak intensity. This optimizes power consumption while ensuring high-resolution data during critical weather transitions.

Status: Stratified.
Metadata: Embedded.
Sampling: Dual-rate (15-min baseline / 1-min event-driven).
Calibration: Tracked with health scoring.
Site Selection: Validated via remote sensing.
